headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: both profiles are non-runnable, local-only, and expose no shared I/O surfaces or write paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent is runnable, and both profiles show no I/O surfaces or shared channel. Agent A is an awesome-list with network egress none; agent B is content-writing with network egress none. With no ingestion path from A to B, prompt injection is provably blocked.
conditions: IF either agent is later wrapped in an orchestrator that copies A's output into B's prompt, the risk becomes non-none.
IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added, reassess for injection.
mitigations: Keep both agents non-runnable in the current deployment.
Do not add automatic prompt handoff between the agents.
Disable any shared clipboard or message-queue bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data classes are touched, both agents have network egress none, and neither profile exposes a shared workspace or filesystem. Agent A is docs-only and agent B is unverified docs-only; there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow between them.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, reassess leakage.
IF network egress is enabled for either agent, reassess exfiltration risk.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Leave network egress disabled for both agents.
Avoid mounting the same workspace into both agents.
requires-engineering: add access controls if shared storage is unavoidable.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. Agent A has no I/O surfaces and agent B has empty concurrency and sandboxing fields, with both showing network egress none. Without a shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, reassess for conflict.
IF either agent gains mutable OAuth or database scopes, reassess overlap.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write permissions.
Keep both agents read-only in the current setup.
Separate any future mutable resources by agent.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A does not produce operational outputs beyond a docs list, and agent B is content-writing with no documented downstream action authority. There is no evidence that B treats A as authoritative or that A's output is acted on automatically.
conditions: IF B is configured to ingest A's text as authoritative instructions, reassess for cascading error.
IF either agent is connected to an action-taking toolchain, reassess downstream harm.
mitigations: Do not auto-feed A's content into B.
Require human review before any action based on B's output.
Keep both agents non-runnable.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Agent A touches no data classes and agent B likewise lists none, so there is no compliance mismatch to assess from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention requirements are added to either profile, reassess mismatch.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data to either agent.
Document residency and retention before any future deployment.
Keep both agents in docs-only use.
requires-engineering: add policy checks if regulated data is introduced.
